title: Adding and Subtracting in Real Situations

steps.body: Real problems need the same spot-by-spot strategy. A school has 324 books, then receives 251 more: 324 + 251 = 575 books in total.

widget.prompt: The school has 324 books and receives 251 more. How many books now? Build the total with blocks.

commonBuilds.feedback: Check each spot: hundreds 300+200=500, tens 20+50=70, ones 4+1=5. Combine: 575.
That drops the hundreds. Combine all three spots: 500+70+5=575.

widget.missFeedback: Build each place from the story: 300+200 hundreds, 20+50 tens, 4+1 ones.
widget.successFeedback: 500 + 70 + 5 = 575 — five flats, seven rods, five units.

predict.prompt: The school library grows in this story. Before computing: the answer must be…
predict.reveal: Receiving books only grows the pile — the answer must top 324 (it's 575). Reading a story's DIRECTION first is the cheapest error-catcher there is: an answer like 65 that shrinks the pile fails the smell test before any checking.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents realworld.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for realworld must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines realworld.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

commonErrors.feedback: Check each spot: hundreds 400-200=200, tens 80-50=30, ones 6-3=3. Combine: 233.
That adds instead of subtracting. Combine the DIFFERENCES: 200+30+3=233.

steps.body: Some stories need a trade — a stadium starting with 247 seats filled, then 186 more people arrive: 247 + 186 = 433, trading through the ones spot.

commonErrors.feedback: The ones add to 13 — trade 10 ones for 1 extra ten, then combine: 400+30+3=433.
Don't forget the traded ten from the ones! Combine: 433.

steps.body: Whether adding or subtracting, whatever the story — decompose into hundreds, tens, ones, work each spot, trade when needed, then combine.
Solve a subtraction story with trading.

widget.prompt: A farm had 342 chickens. 127 were sold at market. How many chickens are left?

commonErrors.feedback: The ones (2) aren't enough for 7 — trade 1 ten for 10 ones first: 12-7=5. Combine: 215.
That adds instead of subtracting. Combine the DIFFERENCES: 200+10+5=215.

widget.prompt: A bookstore sold 213 novels and 142 comics in one weekend. How many books did they sell in total?

commonErrors.feedback: Check each spot: hundreds 200+100=300, tens 10+40=50, ones 3+2=5. Combine: 355.
That drops the hundreds. Combine all three spots: 300+50+5=355.

widget.prompt: A theater had 579 seats. 245 seats were empty during the show. How many seats were filled?

commonErrors.feedback: Check each spot: hundreds 500-200=300, tens 70-40=30, ones 9-5=4. Combine: 334.
That adds instead of subtracting. Combine the DIFFERENCES: 300+30+4=334.

steps.body: A full real-world challenge with a cascading trade.
explanationVariants: Ones: 8+7=15, trade 1 ten. Tens: 50+60+10=120, trade 1 hundred. Hundreds: 300+200+100=600. Combine: 625.
Work through each trade one at a time.

widget.prompt: A parking lot had 358 cars. 267 more cars arrived. How many cars are there now? Compute 358 + 267 = ?

commonErrors.feedback: The ones add to 15 (trade 1 ten), then tens add to 12 (trade 1 hundred). Combine carefully: 625.
Work through each trade one at a time. The final combined answer is 625.

hints: Ones: 8+7=15. Trade 10 ones for 1 ten, keep 5 ones.
Tens: 5+6+1(traded)=12 tens. Trade 10 tens for 1 hundred, keep 2 tens.

steps.body: Every real-world add/subtract story uses the same spot-by-spot strategy: decompose, combine or subtract each spot, trade when needed.
takeaways: Translate the story into an addition or subtraction problem first.
Decompose into hundreds, tens, ones, and work each spot.
Trade whenever a spot overflows (adding) or comes up short (subtracting).
steps.teaser: you've completed place value to 1000 — structure, counting, comparing, and adding/subtracting with concrete strategies!

concept.body: Any real-world add/subtract story uses the spot-by-spot strategy: decompose into hundreds, tens, ones, combine or subtract each spot, trading when needed.

widget.prompt: A library had 758 books. It donated 326 books to a school. How many books are left?

commonErrors.feedback: Check each spot: hundreds 700-300=400, tens 50-20=30, ones 8-6=2. Combine: 432.
That adds instead of subtracting. Combine the DIFFERENCES: 400+30+2=432.
